purpose: Determine whether a detector-triggered commanded action moves the receiver off an impaired timing segment, measured against a matched no-action control on identical topology and identical impairment.
development_exclusion: All V1-V5 captures and the two feasibility spikes are excluded from S11 estimation. No threshold, block rule or condition may change.
mechanism_evidence: spike_two_segment/S11_MECHANISM_PROBE.json - all five capability questions YES; commanded port-down produced port 1 UNCALIBRATED->FAULTY and port 2 LISTENING->UNCALIBRATED, and segment-1 egress collapsed.
topology: Two independent L2 bridges. Master A on segment 1, master B on segment 2. One slaveOnly ptp4l with one port on each segment. Neither slave port may be in MASTER state; a run where one is must be preserved and excluded with that reason.
injected_condition: tc netem delay 100us 200us distribution normal on the segment-1 bridge port. Jitter magnitude is the parameter V5 attributed the observation to. No loss is configured.
commanded_action: ip netns exec <slave_ns> ip link set <segment1 slave port> down, executed once, by the live detector, only on the first NONOVERLAPPING_BLOCK_PERSISTENCE_OBSERVED. This is an externally commanded action. It stops the receiver USING the impaired segment; it does not repair the segment.

action.description: detector fires and executes the command

no_action.description: matched control: identical topology, identical impairment, detector runs and records the trigger but executes nothing

execution_constraints: Interleave action and no_action within each repetition.
Preserve every failed attempt with its reason; never delete a run directory.
Same runner, same detector, same thresholds for both arms.
Do not change the impairment, the settle time or the trial length after the first trial.
primary_outcome: Per run: did the receiver's active timing port move from segment 1 to segment 2, evidenced by a FAULTY transition on port 1 and a LISTENING-to-UNCALIBRATED transition on port 2 in slave.log, corroborated by segment-1 egress packet collapse in the tc counters?
secondary_outcomes: time from detection trigger to action execution result
time from action execution to standby port takeover
whether the detector triggered at all, per run
action command return code, per run

prespecified_interpretation.action_>=4of5_and_no_action_0of5: the commanded action, and not the passage of time or the impairment alone, moves the receiver off the impaired segment under these software conditions
prespecified_interpretation.no_action_>0of5: takeover occurs without the action; the action is not shown to be the cause and the comparison is void pending investigation
prespecified_interpretation.action_<4of5_with_triggers_present: the mechanism is unreliable; report the per-run failure mode, do not retune
prespecified_interpretation.detector_does_not_trigger_in_some_action: a miss; report it against the known sensitivity of roughly 13 of 15 and do not exclude the run
prespecified_interpretation.action_command_returncode_nonzero: execution failure; report the rate separately from detection performance

decision_boundary: S11 can establish only that a commanded action changes which segment the receiver uses, in this emulation. It cannot establish physical clock recovery, service restoration, attack response, or that the action would be correct in a production network. Undoing an injected laboratory impairment is never claimed here; the impairment is left in place throughout.
